i: the person who is speaking or writing
i would argue: used to introduce an opinion you are ready to defend
ice cream: a sweet frozen food made from milk or cream
if: used to say that one thing happens only when another is true
if anything: used to suggest the opposite is more likely
important / crucial / vital: mattering a lot, or being essential to the result
in all fairness: used to be fair when judging someone
in any given: in any particular case you look at
in front of: further forward than something, facing it
in hot water: in trouble with someone in authority
in situ: in its original place rather than being moved
in the same boat: in the same difficult situation as someone else
in the same breath: at almost the same moment, often while saying the opposite
in the wake of: after and because of an event
inbox: the folder where new email or messages arrive
increase / rise / grow: to become larger or greater in number, level or size
insurance card: the card that shows you are covered by an insurer
interest rate: the percentage a bank charges or pays on money
iron clothes: to press clothes with a hot iron to smooth them
it goes without saying: it is so obvious that it needs no mention
it stands to reason: it is logical to expect this
jet lag: tiredness after flying across time zones
jump the gun: to start or decide something too early
jump the line: to go ahead of people who have been waiting longer
keep a promise: to do what you said you would do
keep abreast of: to stay up to date with news or changes
keep an eye on: to watch something carefully for a while
keep in touch: to stay in contact with someone
keep something at bay: to stop something bad from getting closer or winning
keep track of: to follow something so you always know its state
keep up with: to move or progress as fast as someone or something else
key card: a plastic card that opens a hotel room door
kpi: a measured figure that shows how well a goal is being met
lay it on thick: to praise or flatter someone far too much
leave much to be desired: to be quite poor in quality
leave no stone unturned: to try every possible way of finding or doing something
let the cat out of the bag: to reveal a secret by accident
light meal: a small amount of simple food
line manager: the person you report to directly at work
livestream: video sent out as it happens, watched online
living room: the room at home where the family sits together
load the dishwasher: to put the dirty dishes into the dishwasher
log in: to enter your name and password to open an account
log out: to close your account session on a device
look / glance / stare: to direct your eyes, briefly, or for a long fixed time
look after: to take care of someone or something
look forward to: to feel pleased about something that is going to happen
look on the bright side: to think about the good part of a bad situation
look up: to search for a fact or word, or to raise your eyes
loyalty card: a card that collects points each time you shop
